notes: The two groups are not a real problem, so I kept them separate. The booklet really builds two things. One is the car (steps 1-12). The other is the doctor's accessory, a handle plate p8 with gauge tile p21 and yellow slope p51 (step 13 sub-steps), plus the briefcase p29. The doctor minifigure holds them, but the minifigure is not in the piece list. They never click onto the car, so adding a join would invent a connection the manual does not show. The p29-p8 link is only a loose 'held by the minifigure' note.
p14 rests on p61 and p15 on p62, matching the positions. The wheel holders p61/p62 are listed at step 1 with the black plates. The booklet shows them in step 2, but that part is built upside-down.

Low-confidence geometry: the booklet is isometric, so x/y/layer values are estimates. Base p40 is at x=2..13, y=0..3, layer 2, with its top at layer 4. Bumper pieces p41/p42 hang off the front and rear and are joined sideways in other_joins.
Steps count every sub-assembly as its own step, so steps run 1-26. The minifigure page is not counted because its parts are not in the piece list. Both cupboard copies share step 14.
Grille tiles p1/p2, doors p25/p26/p32/p33, wheels, tyres, stickers and the briefcase have no grid position. Their connections are in other_joins.

Positions for p35/p28/p13/p12/p10/p11/p20, the roof and the siren are best readings of the pictures. The booklet does not clearly show where p20 (second 1x2 tile) or the side tiles p5/p6 and plates p23/p24 go. The p43/p44 side sills overlap the end cells of the arches slightly.
Piece-id assignments for same-type copies (p10/p11, p36-39 and so on) are arbitrary within their symmetric positions.
